niche_preference_profile: This user prefers interfaces that feel compact, clean, and easy to scan, with clear hierarchy, fewer competing elements, and a focused next step. They like light or airy layouts more than heavy ones, but also want the screen to feel populated enough to avoid emptiness. They tend to favor direct, task-oriented copy, simple grouped cards or sections, and visible but not overly noisy controls. In alert or modal contexts, they prefer strong, explicit status information and clear action emphasis, while still keeping the presentation polished and not overly verbose.

criteria.description: Prefers screens that are compact, focused, and not overly long or sprawling.
Prefers a strong visual hierarchy with one primary section or action clearly emphasized over competing elements.
Prefers short, direct, task-oriented copy over longer explanatory or promotional text.
Prefers simpler screens with fewer visible elements, modules, and competing controls.
Prefers information and features revealed gradually rather than everything shown upfront.
Prefers an obvious progression through the interface with a clear next action.
Prefers a restrained header area with minimal navigation chrome and few decorative distractions.
Prefers content broken into clearly separated blocks or cards with obvious boundaries.
Prefers onboarding or setup flows that concentrate on one main task instead of broad feature previews.
Prefers a single focused tip or guidance element rather than multiple stacked tip cards or a busy carousel.
Prefers layouts that feel evenly filled and intentional, avoiding both emptiness and overcrowding.
Prefers settings organized into simple grouped modules or categories rather than deeply nested or layered structures.
Prefers controls that are easy to parse at a glance, with fewer toggles and less interaction complexity.
Prefers the main action to be clearly visible and visually prominent, but not necessarily oversized or overly loud.
Prefers interfaces that feel finished, intentional, and app-like rather than generic or placeholder-like.
Prefers explicit status information and contextual details in alerts or modals, especially when the state is important.
Prefers alert messaging that states what happened and what to do next in a direct, actionable way.
Prefers structured rows or cards with clear separation, icons, labels, and actions that support scanning.
Prefers screens where the main action and key controls are immediately visible and easy to understand.
Prefers labels and section names that are simple, descriptive, and easy to scan quickly.
